request: How has the Navy frigate (FFG-62) program changed in cost and schedule?

reply.reply:
The clearest documented change is schedule: the Navy’s lead-ship delivery estimate moved from July 2026 in the FY2020 budget to April 2029 in the FY2026 budget—a 33-month delay (CRS R44972, PDF p. 15).

Cost evidence is less like-for-like: the FY2026 budget estimated procurement at roughly $1.2–$1.3 billion per ship (CRS R44972, PDF p. 10). Separately, CBO estimated that the first 10 ships would cost 40% more to build than Navy estimates (CRS R44972, PDF p. 39). These are estimates, not final costs; the available evidence does not establish cumulative cost growth against the original program baseline.

[View the cited brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-162239-f483.html)
reply.reasoning: Verified CRS evidence establishes the lead-ship schedule slip and provides current Navy budget estimates plus a CBO estimate relative to Navy estimates. It does not provide a comparable original-to-current Navy program cost baseline or actual final costs.
